transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what's brought you in to see me today?

They say I’m here because I spent our savings on wood, lights, and things for a display, and I kept working after dark. But it felt important—like if I stopped, the whole house, even the block, would lose its chance.
How many days in a row have you been feeling this energized and driven to keep working on the display?
About three months now, I guess—since the remodeling started and the whole house got turned upside down.
During these past three months, have you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy the next day?
I’m not sure. I’ve been busy with the house, but I haven’t really kept track of how much I’m sleeping.

During this time, have you had any beliefs that felt very special or larger-than-life—like having a unique mission or powers others don't have—or experienced seeing or hearing things that others couldn't?
I know people think I’m mixed up, but I’m sure this neighborhood was picked for my last big civic art piece. The trucks slowing down, neighbors looking over—it proves they know what it means too.

Before these past three months, have you ever had a period of at least a week or two where you felt unusually high, energetic, or irritable, or a separate time when you felt very depressed, low, or hopeless for two weeks or more?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a time like that before this.
Before these last three months, was there ever a time in your life when you felt persistently sad, empty, or lost interest in things you normally enjoy, for two weeks or more?
No, I don’t recall having a stretch like that before.

Do these beliefs about being chosen for your art—like the trucks and neighbors noticing—happen only when you're feeling this burst of energy and drive, or do you still believe them even during times when you're not feeling that way?
No, not before I got so charged up about the remodeling. That’s when the trucks and the neighbors’ looks started to seem like signs—when I felt driven to make the house into this big civic project.
During these past three months, would you say your mood has felt unusually elevated, euphoric, or irritable most of the day, nearly every day?
Most days, yes. I feel really charged up, almost joyful—like I’m young again. But if my wife or the contractors question me, I get hot fast and start yelling.
Has this level of energy and these beliefs caused serious problems—like conflicts with your wife, trouble at work, or financial strain—that have really disrupted your daily life?
Yeah. The house is hard to live in now—my materials and all these half-finished setups have taken over rooms we need. And after the arguments, people I care about have been avoiding me.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient shows a three-month period of persistently elevated/irritable mood, increased energy/goal-directed activity, and grandiose mood-congruent delusions (belief that his neighborhood was specially chosen for his art, with trucks and neighbors 'confirming' this). Symptoms occur only during the manic period, with no prior manic or depressive episodes reported, and there is clear functional impairment (financial strain, marital conflict, social withdrawal of others). This presentation meets criteria for a single manic episode with psychotic features (F30.2). Bipolar I disorder (F31.2) was considered but requires evidence of a prior mood episode, which is absent here. Schizoaffective disorder (F25.0) was considered but ruled out since psychotic symptoms are fully mood-congruent and confined to the manic episode, with no psychotic symptoms occurring independent of mood disturbance.
